title: Auto-generated adaptive hydraulic lookup preflight
question: Can a self-generated branch-aware hydraulic representation reduce repeated constitutive evaluation cost while preserving the authoritative B1.10 hydraulic response closely enough for a later end-to-end Richards qualification?
hypothesis: A build-once, freeze-for-run representation can concentrate support points where theta, capacity and conductivity are difficult, use exact cheap branches where lookup adds no value, and therefore outperform a uniformly resolved lookup at comparable constitutive error.

mandatory_semantic_boundaries: conductivity saturation switch when inside the represented interval
capacity-floor kink when inside the represented interval
direct_exact_regions: near-saturation branch Hcrit < h < 0 in this preflight

later_required_gates_before_any_producti: independent dense constitutive validation including one-sided branch limits
comparison against the current fixed-table research baseline
end-to-end Richards hydrological equivalence on the hydraulic test bank
explicit qualification of any additional hydraulic model family
decision_rule: Advance only if the adaptive/hybrid representation shows a material reduction in representation work or point count at comparable error and remains suitable for a later end-to-end solver benchmark.
